cand.title: Strengthening Capacity in Global Health Diplomacy
cand.organizationName: International Geneva Global Health Platform / Geneva Graduate Institute
cand.excerpt: Strong official event evidence and credible scientific/education demand mechanism; venue commitment prevents treating it as open inventory.
cand.ledgerVenue: Global Health Centre, Geneva Graduate Institute

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two verified relevant organizer contacts, not verified hotel buyers: Angèle Flora Mendy, Capacity Building Coordinator, Global Health Centre, is the best first operational contact for participant geography and lodging/referral questions; Daniela Morich, Head of Policy Engagement & Global Health Platform, is the relevant platform-level relationship contact. Relevance is inferred from their published responsibilities; neither is proven to control hotel procurement. The programme publishes globalhealth@graduateinstitute.ch as its enquiry route. The Platform team page spells the coordinator’s surname “Mendi”; the Institute’s individual profile uses “Mendy”, used here.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced 2027 in-person programme in Geneva, Switzerland: first activity 10 February 2027, last scheduled activity 21 October 2027. Actual modules: 10–12 February, The New Diplomacy of Global Health; 18 March, Geopolitics and Global Health Diplomacy; 23–24 June, Global Health Law; 6–7 July, Negotiation Skills for Global Health Diplomacy; 14–15 September, Climate Change & Global Health Diplomacy; 21 October, The Global Health Ecosystem for Access to Medicines. These are intermittent sessions, not a continuous February–October residential stay. The foundational course is three half-days, short courses two half-days, and master classes 2–3 hours. Although described generically as a 12-month programme, only these 2027 activity dates are published. No official 2028 edition announcement was found. The 2026 cycle ends on 1 December 2026, before the requested horizon.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied YOTEL product constraints: weak primary fit, with only conditional ancillary lodging potential. The programme is explicitly designed for Geneva-based stakeholders; outside-Switzerland applicants are accepted, but the travelling share is unpublished. Classes remain at the Institute in Geneva city, whereas YOTEL is in Founex. Its 237 guestrooms and six meeting rooms do not establish demand or justify a 20–120-room block. A referral rate for genuinely non-local participants could be explored only if their travel plans and willingness to commute are confirmed. No support for a resort/retreat relocation, full-house booking, banquet business or continuous extended-stay cohort. No published attendance, peak rooms or room nights was found; size suitability cannot be quantified. No edition-specific Geneva Airport arrival or La Côte lodging evidence was found.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: “Global Health Centre, Graduate Institute for International and Development Studies, Geneva”; the programme explicitly “will take place in person at the Geneva Graduate Institute throughout 2027.” City: Geneva; region: Canton of Geneva; country: Switzerland. Territory classification: Geneva city, not Founex/Nyon/La Côte/Geneva Airport corridor. The Centre’s published contact address is Maison de la paix, Chemin Eugène-Rigot 2A, CH-1211 Genève 1; no edition-specific classroom or auditorium is identified. This is a confirmed institutional venue, not a competing hotel or evidence of a hotel-room commitment.
findings.historicalRotation: The official prior-cycle page publishes 2026 sessions on 5 March, 18–20 March, 24–25 June, 7 July, 7–8 October, 3 November and 1 December, all under an in-person Geneva Graduate Institute programme. As of 17 November 2026 this prior cycle is not wholly historical: its final session is still upcoming but outside the requested horizon. Its calendar header shows 5–6 March 2026, which does not represent the full activity schedule; the body is the appropriate date evidence. The 2027 programme again commits to the Institute in Geneva. Two consecutive cycles are verified; no destination or hotel rotation is established, and no earlier edition of this exact programme was verified.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Official wording: “Participants traveling from outside Geneva must cover their own travel and accommodation costs and arrange for their own visas where needed.” This establishes participant-funded accommodation, not who books it. No edition-specific housing bureau, host hotel, named hotel, room block, booking link, open hotel RFP or contracted inventory was found in the programme pages or linked 2027 schedule. Hotels listed for this edition: none found. Booking channel and any unpublished arrangements remain unknown; do not mark hotel sourcing open or committed elsewhere.
findings.organizationStructure: Academic capacity-building programme offered by the International Geneva Global Health Platform, hosted by the Global Health Centre at the Geneva Graduate Institute, with support from the Institute of Philanthropy. The Platform is an institutional convening/capacity-building initiative, not evidenced here as an independent membership association, corporate event agency, PCO or DMC. The Institute is both host institution and published teaching venue; the philanthropic supporter is not thereby a lodging buyer. No appointed external accommodation intermediary is identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The material competitive constraints are the already designated academic teaching venue, a Geneva-based target audience and short, dispersed sessions. No incumbent hotel, competing room block, hotel sell-out or overflow demand was found. The Institute is not a competing hotel. Do not infer overflow from Geneva’s wider events market, or assume accommodation availability merely because no contract is published.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Use the published programme inbox, globalhealth@graduateinstitute.ch, requesting routing to Angèle Flora Mendy and, for platform-level discussion, Daniela Morich. Ask after selection (notifications due by 10 December 2026) how many 2027 participants will travel, which modules require nights, who makes hotel bookings, and whether any accommodation agreements or referral channels already exist. Offer a non-exclusive lodging discussion only if a genuine non-local need and acceptable Founex commute are confirmed. Do not lead with a meeting-room bid, reserve a speculative block, or assume meal/catering capacity. If no travelling cohort exists, retain a low-priority institutional relationship rather than a dated hotel-demand opportunity.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the next edition, 2027 meeting space is not an evidenced open opportunity: teaching is assigned to the Institute. Participant-funded lodging creates a possible enquiry/referral path, but no open group block or booking authority is established. The published application deadline was 8 November 2026, already passed on the research date; selection notifications are due by 10 December 2026. A lodging-needs enquiry around selection is more appropriate than an application or venue-replacement pitch. No direct access to participant lists is implied.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Two successive programme cycles support a recurring relationship-development thesis, not a verified annual open bidding cycle. No 2028 dates or venue were found. Inference: seek permission to be considered for non-local participant accommodation or separately commissioned training/retreat needs, without assuming that Institute-based classes will rotate off-site. Future competitive capture is conditional on an identified travelling cohort and a sourcing decision; it is not currently qualified inventory.
